text: /// A registry is a trust root, so `use`-ing something it already offers is a
/// no-op rather than a recorded entry.
/// Record an enablement for `name` and sync so its skills install now.
// `disable` outranks every way of enabling a plugin, `use` included, so
// recording an entry here would report success and then install nothing.
// Re-enabling is dropping the `disable` entry, which is a deliberate edit
// rather than something `use` undoes on the user's behalf.
bail!("`{name}` is disabled in `[plugins] disable`; remove that entry to enable it again");
// A configured registry is a trust root: what it offers is already
// enabled by configuration, so there is nothing to record. The exception
// is a dormant plugin, for which `use` is exactly the wake-up call.
"`{name}` is already available from a configured registry; nothing to enable"
message: format!("`{name}` is already enabled; nothing changed"),
// Install now rather than waiting for the next sync.

rationale:
In `use_plugin`, after resolving `name` to an identity `id`, the loaded registry plugins are searched for one whose `pms.identity(&p.canonical) == id`. If one exists and is not dormant (`!manifest.requires_use`), the function reports that the plugin is already available from a configured registry and returns `Ok(())` before building an entry, saving config, or syncing. The code treats every non-dormant registry plugin as already enabled (a superset of "already activates"), so it records nothing whenever the requirement asks it to; a dormant plugin is recorded, which is the `use_wakes_dormant` case and not covered by this requirement. If `[plugins] disable` also names the plugin, the earlier disable check fails instead, which still records nothing.

Test (passes): `use_registry_content_is_a_noop` runs `use serde-guidance` against the `plugins0` registry fixture and asserts the config does not mention it.
requirement: `cargo agents use <name>` MUST record nothing when a configured registry already activates the named plugin.
